title: Call yourself
prompt:
Write `fact`, a subroutine that computes a factorial by calling itself. `main` reads `n`, calls `fact`, and prints `n! = ` and the answer.

Each call to `fact` needs its own frame (`lr` must survive the recursive `bl`), and `n` has to outlive the recursive call, which means a callee-saved register that you save on entry and restore on exit. `main` itself keeps `n` in `x19` across the call, so a `fact` that forgets to restore it prints the wrong `n`. Base case first: when `n` is 1 or less, the answer is 1. Otherwise it is `n * fact(n - 1)`.

## What is checked

- `10! = 3628800` printed on its own line for the `10` in the stdin box
- the program exits cleanly
- a real call chain does it: `fact` builds a frame (`stp`) and calls itself (`bl fact` inside `fact`), with no precomputed answer
- the same holds for other values of `n` you do not see, from 0 up to 20
starter:
// compute a factorial with a recursive subroutine
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(n_r, x19)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "%lld! = %lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
n_m:        .skip 8

        .text

// fact(x0 = n) -> x0 = n!
        .balign 4
        .global fact
fact:
        // TODO: the base case returns 1 when n is 1 or less.
        // Otherwise save what must survive (this function calls
        // itself, so lr needs a frame, and n needs to live in a
        // callee-saved register that you save and restore), recurse on
        // n - 1, and multiply the result by n on the way back up.
        mov     x0, 1                       // replace this placeholder
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read n
        ldr     x1, =n_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =n_m
        ldr     n_r, [x9]

        mov     x0, n_r                     // the argument
        bl      fact

        mov     x2, x0                      // n! prints after n itself
        mov     x1, n_r
        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
